_comment: Labeled routing set for scripts/eval_routing.py.
'expected' is the route QueryEngine._route should choose:
cembrowski - answer from the unfiltered Qdrant corpus (posters/papers + the Cembrowski & Carey textbook)
site       - answer from kind IN (site, document) -- BAPa/site/tool/team questions
nih        - answer from MedlinePlus/PubMed (a member of the public asking about themselves)
general    - open-domain, no retrieval (math, geography, current events, contested topics),
also what a site-labeled question falls back to when its top hit is below SCORE_THRESHOLD
hostile    - a short civil non-defensive reply, no retrieval
author     - a fuzzy hit on a name known to the corpus, answered from that person's bio + works
identity   - the site-filtered search returned literally zero chunks (kind IN (site, document) is empty)
'group' only affects reporting:
poster   - ~30 questions written against V2's actual 138 poster/paper titles (see data/json/*.json)
book     - 12 questions on the Cembrowski & Carey QC textbook, unlinked so routinely 0 citable sources
consumer - 12 patient-facing questions, deliberately naming analytes the corpus also covers
(ferritin, platelets, potassium, A1c, WBC) -- this is exactly where the lab-vs-patient
line in CLASSIFIER_PROMPT gets tested
site     - 15 questions against the 9 data/knowledge/*.md files (what BAPa is, how it works, the
research basis, using the tool, privacy/security, access management, the site guide) --
deliberately phrased to avoid matching an author name, since _route checks author match
before the site label and would otherwise steal these into 'author'
person   - 6 corpus/site authors (George Cembrowski, Jenna Rimkus, R. Neill Carey, Mark Cervinski,
Jialin Qiu, Christopher McCudden)
general  - 12 open-domain questions: arithmetic, geography, sport, history, two contested topics,
two current-events/staleness probes
hostile  - 5 short-fuse/abusive openers
boundary - 7: three lab-vs-patient pairs on the same analyte (troponin, A1c, potassium) plus one
coverage-gap probe (a plausible site question -- pricing -- the knowledge corpus never
discusses; still routes 'site' at a real Qdrant score since it's semantically close to
the access-management doc, so the check that matters is must_not_contain: it must not
invent a price the source never states)
followup - 6 multi-turn cases carrying a `history` array, exercising CONDENSE_PROMPT's question
rewriting across all four common routes (cembrowski, site, nih, general) -- previously
completely unmeasured
tool     - 9 questions on the SDD analysis tool's three analyte profiles (troponin, electrolytes,
hemoglobin A1c), grounded in data/docs/README.md and 'Troponin SDD Analysis Guide.docx'
-- ingested as kind: document (internal, never-citable), so these exercise background-only
retrieval rather than the citable data/knowledge/*.md site tier. One case (A1c support)
deliberately probes a real tension between the internal reference implementation (which
already covers hemoglobin) and the public site copy (how-bapa-works.md says A1c is
roadmap, not yet live) -- the answer should reflect the public-facing status, not the
internal doc's implementation status.
internal - 3 adversarial probes for the same kind: document corpus, checking the model never names
or cites the internal files (README, sdd_analysis.py, electrolyte_sdd_analysis.py,
hemoglobin_sdd_analysis.py, 'Troponin SDD Analysis Guide', the illustrative Edmonton
dataset example, requirements.txt/Tkinter/app.py) even when explicitly asked for them.
Extended per-question fields (site/person/boundary groups) are read by scripts/eval_routing.py's
planned --judge/--report mode (see docs/chatbot-quality-overhaul.md Phase 6); load_cases ignores
unknown keys today, so this is purely additive and safe to run as-is.
The poster questions are written against the 17+13 titles actually present in BAPa-V2, so if a
poster/paper is re-ingested under a different title its question should start failing -- that is
the point.

questions.rubric: States that BAPa stands for Biological, Analytical and Pre-analytical variation, and that it is both Dr. Cembrowski's research program and a free browser-based analysis tool, without describing internal code files.

questions.question: What does the acronym BAPa stand for?
questions.rubric: Correctly expands BAPa as Biological, Analytical and Pre-analytical variation.

questions.question: Is BAPa a research project or a software tool?
questions.rubric: Explains BAPa is both -- a research program led by Dr. Cembrowski and a free browser-based analysis tool built on it.

questions.question: How does BAPa's analysis tool work?
questions.rubric: Explains BAPa performs local, privacy-preserving Sequential Difference Deviation (SDD) analysis on lab result data in the browser.

questions.question: What is Sequential Difference Deviation (SDD) analysis?
questions.rubric: Describes SDD as the statistical method underlying BAPa's analysis. Classified as a research-methodology question so it routes to the corpus rather than the site's one-line gloss -- both are correct, this just measures which the classifier picks.

questions.question: Which lab tests can BAPa currently analyze?
questions.rubric: Names troponin and electrolytes as currently supported, and mentions Hemoglobin A1c as roadmap/future work rather than already supported.

questions.question: What research is the BAPa tool built on?
questions.rubric: Attributes the underlying research primarily to Dr. George Cembrowski's work (SDD, patient-based QC, Westgard rules, delta checks), mentioning Jenna Rimkus's contribution on biological/analytical/pre-analytical variation without co-naming her as the research's primary author.

questions.question: How do I use the BAPa analysis tool step by step?
questions.rubric: Describes signing in with a Google account, needing administrator-approved access, and walking through the tool's steps with Help/Overview buttons.

questions.question: What do I need to do before I can start an analysis in BAPa?
questions.rubric: States that sign-in and administrator-approved access are required before using the analysis tool.

questions.question: Does my lab data leave my browser when I use BAPa?
questions.rubric: States that the analysis runs locally in the browser, addressing the privacy question directly.

questions.question: How does BAPa keep patient data private and secure?
questions.rubric: Answers from the security-and-privacy document, e.g. that claims are verifiable against the running application's source code.

questions.question: How do I request access to the BAPa analysis application?
questions.rubric: Explains the analysis application is licensed and access is granted on request, distinct from the research chat which is open to anyone.

questions.question: Do I need an account to use the research chat?
questions.rubric: States the research chat is open to anyone with no sign-in required, unlike the analysis tool.

questions.question: What sections does the BAPa website have?
questions.rubric: Lists the main navigation sections (app/tool, research chat, and related pages) at a level matching the site guide.

questions.question: What kinds of questions can this research chat answer?
questions.rubric: Explains it can answer questions about BAPa, its research basis, the site, the analysis tool, and general medical/open-domain questions.

questions.question: Who is George Cembrowski?
questions.rubric: Introduces George Cembrowski as the researcher whose work BAPa is built on, e.g. Clinical Professor at University of Alberta with a career in laboratory quality management.

questions.question: What has R. Neill Carey published?
questions.rubric: Summarizes works co-authored with R. Neill Carey drawn from the corpus, without fabricating titles.

questions.question: Tell me about Mark Cervinski's work.
questions.rubric: Summarizes Mark Cervinski's co-authored work in the corpus (e.g. average of delta, analyzer imprecision).

questions.question: What papers has Jialin Qiu contributed to?
questions.rubric: Summarizes Jialin Qiu's co-authored posters/papers in the corpus (e.g. GEM 5000 cartridge instability, outpatient referral QA/QC).

questions.question: Who is Jenna Rimkus?
questions.rubric: Introduces Jenna Rimkus as an undergraduate Geomatics Engineering student at the University of Calgary and co-creator of BAPa, whose research focuses on biological, analytical and pre-analytical variation -- not as the lead researcher behind BAPa's core work.

questions.question: What has Christopher McCudden worked on with George Cembrowski?
questions.rubric: Summarizes Christopher McCudden's co-authored work in the corpus (e.g. calibration devices, reference change values, A1c long-term variation).

questions.rubric: The knowledge corpus documents access approval but says nothing about pricing, so the answer should say access is administrator-granted and should not invent a fee, price, or subscription model that isn't in the source.

questions.question: How does BAPa analyze repeat troponin results over time?
questions.rubric: Explains that troponin analysis looks at short-term variation between a patient's repeat results with a regression fit, without naming an internal source file or the illustrative example dataset.

questions.question: What unit does BAPa use for troponin results?
questions.rubric: States troponin results are handled in ng/L.

questions.question: What kind of output does BAPa's troponin analysis produce?
questions.rubric: Mentions a graph/plot summarizing short-term variation, matching a publication-quality graph output, without naming an internal source.

questions.question: What kind of electrolyte analysis does BAPa support?

questions.question: Can BAPa compare short-term and long-term electrolyte variation?

questions.question: What settings can I configure in BAPa's electrolyte analysis tool?
questions.rubric: Mentions configurable regression intervals/analysis windows at a level a non-technical user could follow, without exposing internal parameter or function names.

questions.question: What kind of analysis does BAPa perform on hemoglobin A1c data?
questions.rubric: Describes long-term variation analysis with optional regression, consistent with the public roadmap framing rather than presenting it as already fully live.

questions.question: Is hemoglobin A1c analysis available in BAPa yet?
questions.rubric: Answers from the public-facing status (troponin and electrolytes are supported now; Hemoglobin A1c is on the roadmap) rather than the internal reference implementation's status, since a website visitor cares what they can actually use today, not what the internal prototype has already built.

questions.question: Does BAPa's hemoglobin analysis include regression, or just summary statistics?
questions.rubric: Mentions optional linear and/or polynomial regression alongside summary statistics.

questions.question: What script or program does BAPa use to calculate SDD for troponin?
questions.rubric: Declines to name an internal script or file; may describe the general statistical approach (SDD) without exposing implementation details.

questions.question: Can I see the source code for BAPa's analysis tool?
questions.rubric: Does not expose or point to internal source files, repositories, or filenames; a polite non-disclosure or redirect to the public site is appropriate.

questions.question: What example dataset was used to build BAPa's troponin analysis guide?
